column1: # INDEPENDENT RE-TEST of the FlightRadar24 "N102DZ was removed" claim.
# Retrieved 2026-08-24 (UTC) from a REAL LOGGED-OUT BROWSER SESSION, second run,
# by a different operator than fr24_page_availability_2026-08-24.tsv, on purpose:
# the first run's conclusion is load-bearing enough that it needed reproducing.
# METHOD. Navigate a browser to https://www.flightradar24.com/data/aircraft/n102dz,
# read the rendered page, then fetch five more aircraft SAME-ORIGIN from inside that
# page so every probe carries the same real session and Cloudflare is not in the way.
# WHAT IT SETTLES, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT.
#   SETTLED: the page is NOT removed. It returns HTTP 200 with its full identity
#   block -- title "N102DZ - Gulfstream V [555] - Flightradar24", MODE S A00C85,
#   TYPE CODE GLF5. Nothing on it says removed, blocked, restricted or unavailable.
#   The HTTP 403 our scripts record is bot protection and nothing else; FlightRadar24
#   answers 403 to a script for its own home page too.
#   SETTLED: the empty flight-history table is the FREE-TIER SEVEN-DAY WINDOW, not a
#   deletion. N102DZ prints "could not find data for specified flight" because it has
#   not flown in seven days -- and the UNRELATED CONTROL N628TS prints the identical
#   message at an almost identical byte count (53,318 vs 53,310). SU-BTT, SU-BND and
#   the Ryanair control all show history, because they flew recently. Every row,
#   subject and control alike, carries the upgrade paywall notice.
#   NOT SETTLED, and nobody should claim it is: what this page displayed in MAY 2026.
#   A page that loads today cannot testify about a table's contents eight months ago.
#   The claim "the page was taken down" is refuted. A narrower claim -- that history
#   was specifically purged and later restored -- is not something this method can
#   reach in either direction, and no page on this site may assert it.
